root.name: Dutch Defense: Bladel Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Nh6

overview: Black plays a Leningrad-style 1...f5 and ...g6 but puts the knight on h6 (probably heading for f7) instead of g8-f6, keeping the f-pawn and e-pawn flexible. White develops with Nc3 and can take the bishop pair with Bxh6 or build the usual g3/Bg2 or e4 set-up. I am not certain of the theory, so this is read from the moves and the parent Dutch.

white_ideas.idea: Bxh6 to damage structure or take the bishop pair
Fianchetto with g3, Bg2 and Nf3, or strike with e4

black_ideas.idea: Reroute the knight to f7 and play ...Bg7, ...O-O

typical_structures.structure: Leningrad-type Dutch with Black pawns on f5, g6, d6

character.notes: Dutch Leningrad style, double-edged with a loosened kingside; the rim knight adds risk for Black.

gambit.notes: No material is offered; 3...Nh6 is a developing move.

soundness.notes: Playable but a slow, slightly awkward set-up; White gets Bxh6 options.

structure.notes: Pawn centre not yet fixed; both sides keep options (…e5 or …d6/…e5, or e4 for White).

approach.notes: Rare Dutch sideline that strong players seldom pick.

level.notes: Plans are Leningrad-like and not heavy on theory but need understanding of Dutch weaknesses.

character.reason: The Dutch Leningrad set-up gives unbalanced, double-edged play with a weakened kingside.

soundness.reason: The knight on h6 is slightly awkward but Black is not worse by force.

structure.reason: The centre is not fixed after three moves and either e4 or ...e5 can follow.

approach.reason: The Bladel is a rare Dutch sideline that strong players hardly choose.

level.reason: It asks for Dutch-type understanding but has little forcing theory.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes and fights for e4 and e5 with pieces.
